example: A flicker of hope returned after the call.
figurativeMeaning: A brief sign of an emotion

definition: To gradually disappear or lose strength.
example: The memory began to fade away over time.

definition: To leave or be lost quietly.
example: The opportunity slipped away before he acted.
figurativeMeaning: An opportunity or moment is lost

definition: To make something impossible to hear by being louder.
example: The crowd drowned out the announcement.
figurativeMeaning: To overwhelm or suppress a thought or feeling

definition: To stop paying attention.
example: I tend to tune out when the explanation gets repetitive.

definition: To stop concentrating and become unaware of surroundings.
example: I zoned out halfway through the lecture.

definition: Surprised when unprepared.
example: The question caught me off guard.

arabic: منفصل عن الواقع أو غير مطّلع
definition: Unaware of current feelings or situations.
example: The policy felt out of touch with students' needs.

definition: Feeling or appearing unsuitable in a setting.
example: I felt out of place at the formal event.

arabic: يشاهد من الخارج دون شعور بالانتماء
definition: Feeling excluded while observing others' experiences.
example: At the reunion, he felt like he was outside looking in.

definition: To do something mechanically without feeling involved.
example: He was just going through the motions at work.

definition: To appear cheerful or calm despite difficulty.
example: She put on a brave face during the farewell.

definition: To stay emotionally controlled.
example: He tried to keep it together during the speech.

definition: To forget what you were about to say.
example: I lost my train of thought when the phone rang.

arabic: يستفز شخصًا أو يؤثر فيه بعمق
definition: To annoy or affect someone strongly.
example: That criticism really got under his skin.

definition: To have a lasting effect.
example: The experience left a mark on everyone involved.

definition: To cause ongoing worry or sadness.
example: The unfinished conversation weighed on her.

definition: To gradually damage or consume something.
example: Doubt began to eat away at his confidence.

definition: Unable to choose between competing feelings or options.
example: She was torn between staying and leaving.

definition: Very different from something else.
example: The final result was a far cry from the original idea.

definition: Not completely or exactly.
example: That's not quite what I meant.

definition: Usually, though not always.
example: More often than not, the simplest explanation is right.

definition: Used to offer an opinion without insisting on it.
example: For what it's worth, I think you handled it well.

definition: Partly, but not completely.
example: I agree with that point to some extent.

definition: Used to give enthusiastic permission.
example: By all means, ask another question.

definition: Used when changing an earlier decision.
example: On second thought, let's leave a little earlier.

arabic: مع ذلك أو رغم ما سبق
definition: Used to introduce a contrasting point.
example: The design is simple; that being said, it works well.

definition: Used when revealing an unexpected fact.
example: As it turns out, we had met before.

definition: To make a special effort.
example: She went out of her way to help the new student.

definition: To feel that criticism is directed at you.
example: Try not to take the feedback personally.

word: Give someone the benefit of the doubt
definition: To trust someone when the facts are uncertain.
example: I gave him the benefit of the doubt at first.

definition: To reveal a great deal indirectly.
example: Her silence spoke volumes about her disappointment.

definition: The feeling of being accepted as part of a group.
example: The club gave new students a sense of belonging.
